title: next_id() read-then-write race: concurrent GUI/CLI/agent writers raise unhandled sqlite3.IntegrityError, silently dropping chat messages and habit creations
description: next_id() (habit_core.py:111-115) does SELECT v FROM meta, then INSERT OR REPLACE next_id=n+1, as two separate statements with no BEGIN IMMEDIATE — a classic read-then-write TOCTOU across connections. The deployment is explicitly concurrent by design (WAL + busy_timeout=5000 set in connect() for 'concurrent CLI/GUI/agent' use), and busy_timeout does not serialize this: two connections can both SELECT the same next_id value before either commits its meta write, so both compute the same id; the second INSERT into habits(id)/chat(id) (both INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, no AUTOINCREMENT) fails with IntegrityError. add_habit (line 244) and post_chat (line 454) both allocate ids this way. The exception then escapes every handler: cli() catches only (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) (habit_core.py:1058) so `habitctl add`/`chat send` die with a raw traceback and the write is lost; on the GUI side Bridge.sendChat (habit_gui.py:149-154) catches nothing and Bridge.addHabit catches only ValueError, so the IntegrityError propagates into the QML slot — with PySide6 6.11 the app survives but the human's chat message or habit is silently dropped with no feedback (verified by execution on PySide6 6.11.0: an unhandled exception in a C++-invoked slot prints a traceback and the event loop continues). Reproduced by execution: two concurrent add_habit calls on one WAL DB -> one succeeds, the other raises 'IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: habits.id' (see repro harness output). This also violates the project's own mandated SQLite rule (AGENTS.md: 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE for read-then-write'). Impact: lost operator chat messages at the exact moment the operator is talking to the agent (the GUI chat send racing any agent-side add/chat write is the normal steady state), failed habit creations with traceback instead of error message, and a corrupted-looking audit trail. Not a DoS finding: it is a data-loss/concurrency correctness flaw on the designed hot path.
repro_hints: Repro harness: C:/Users/ala/AppData/Local/Temp/mantis_repro/repro.py section 'F-03 next_id race' — thread A holds BEGIN EXCLUSIVE briefly while two threads call core.add_habit(); on release, one thread raises IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: habits.id (observed). No repo files touched, temp DB only. Fix shape: wrap next_id in BEGIN IMMEDIATE (per the project sqlite skill) or use an UPDATE ... RETURNING / AUTOINCREMENT counter.
reasoning: Verified against habit_core.py:111 (next_id). Old code did SELECT-then-INSERT OR REPLACE across two statements with no transaction bracket — TOCTOU confirmed by execution in the Mantis repro harness (F-03 section): two concurrent add_habit calls on one WAL DB produced 'IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: habits.id'. A second latent bug in the same function surfaced during this session: the meta UPDATE bound a bare string '(str(n+1))' (no tuple), so sqlite3 read the string's characters as bindings and crashed the moment the counter hit 10 (live DB sat at next_id=6). BOTH are fixed by the atomic UPSERT now landed at the same site (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE + in-transaction SELECT, SQLite 3.24+ compatible). Verified: sequential ids 1..12, migration from v=6, and 3 rounds x 16 threads of concurrent add_habit/post_chat on WAL — 48/48 unique ids, zero IntegrityErrors. AGENTS.md sqlite rule ('BEGIN IMMEDIATE for read-then-write') satisfied via the single-statement write-lock approach; ruff + pytest green.
